title.rendered: Declaring Against the Enemy: Resist and He Will Flee | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 12

excerpt.rendered: James tells us to resist the devil and he will flee. Jesus gave us authority to tread on serpents. Day 12 teaches believers how to declare in spiritual warfare, in the authority of Jesus, not in bravado.

content.rendered:
Spiritual warfare is not a shouting match. Jesus authorised believers to speak with calm, settled, Scripture-anchored authority, and promised that the enemy would flee.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, October 29, 2026 | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 12

Today’s Scripture

“Therefore submit to God. Resist the devil and he will flee from you.”
James 4:7 (NKJV)

“Behold, I give you the authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you.”
Luke 10:19 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

James 4:7 gives us the order of warfare. The NKJV says, “Submit to God. Resist the devil.” The AMPC expands it: “So be subject to God. Resist the devil [stand firm against him], and he will flee from you.” The TPT renders Luke 10:19: “Now you understand that I have imparted to you my authority to trample over his kingdom.” Jesus is not sending His Church to fight for victory; He is sending His Church to enforce a victory already won at Calvary.

Spiritual warfare has become fashionable, and some of it has become theatrical. True declaration against the enemy is quiet, Scripture-anchored, and in the Name of Jesus, not in volume, not in anger, not in bravado. From Lagos to London, Manila to Nairobi to São Paulo, believers are learning that the devil does not flee from loud people; he flees from submitted people. Submission to God is the throne under the sword. Without it, the sword has no weight. With it, even a whisper in Jesus’ name makes hell tremble.

Jesus Himself showed us the pattern. In the wilderness, He did not scream at the devil. He simply said, three times, “It is written” (Matthew 4). On the Mount of Olives, He did not panic in the garden; He prayed and declared His submission. On the cross, He did not improvise; He quoted Scripture and consummated the victory. “Having disarmed principalities and powers, He made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them in it” (Colossians 2:15). We do not fight for that victory. We stand in it.

So in your home, declare it. In your workplace, declare it. Over your children, declare it. When fear tries to flood your bedroom at 2 a.m., declare it. When the lion roars (1 Peter 5:8), remember Jesus is the Lion of Judah, and the lesser lion has already been defeated. Resist in Jesus’ name. He will flee. He has to.

The Pattern of Declaration

Acknowledge. Jesus has already won. Calvary stripped the enemy of legal authority. We enforce the victory; we do not negotiate for it.

Personalise. Name the specific pressure. Fear. Depression. A spirit of lust. A spirit of poverty. A generational pattern. Call it out by Scripture, not by hype.

Proclaim. Submit, then resist. In Jesus’ name. Quote the Word. Speak once with authority rather than ten times in panic.

Declaration

I declare and acknowledge that I am submitted to God, and the devil flees from me. Jesus has given me authority to trample on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt me. The accuser of the brethren has no legal case in my life, because the blood of Jesus has settled every charge. I bind every demonic strategy against my mind, my body, my family, my work, and my ministry. I loose the angels of the Lord to encamp around me and mine. Fear, you have no seat at my table. Confusion, you have no voice over my steps. Lies, you have no root in my spirit. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
